reviewedInclusionSources.evidence_summary: Global Pass column explicitly includes Eurostar ES; DB ICE and international ICE; ÖBB RailJet RJ/RJX and international carriers. One Country Pass restrictions are a different column. Slovenia Railjet Global Pass is X: Slovenia is excluded from this map review.

reviewedInclusionSources.quote: Note these passes are not valid on Eurostar Snow trains.
reviewedInclusionSources.evidence_summary: Operator confirms Eurail/Interrail acceptance for ordinary continental and London services with a passholder fare or mandatory paid seat reservation. Snow is excluded. Operator FAQ booking-channel details differ from current pass website: no booking-channel instructions are inferred.

reviewedInclusionSources.quote: Travellers with a 2nd class Pass can only travel in Eurostar Standard.
reviewedInclusionSources.evidence_summary: Mandatory reservations, limited passholder availability, no Eurostar Premier. London services require Global Pass. Current map review covers named Amsterdam–London and Paris–Amsterdam ordinary corridors only.

International ICE routes are listed to Austria, Belgium, France, Netherlands and Switzerland. France routes require reservations year-round; certain Netherlands and Belgium international summer periods require reservations. This review is bounded to 1–7 November 2026, outside the stated summer dates.

reviewedInclusionSources.quote: However, when travelling in or to Hungary, reservations are compulsory.
reviewedInclusionSources.evidence_summary: Railjet international routes explicitly connect Austria with Germany, Switzerland, Hungary and Czechia. Ordinary second class reviewed only. Business-class upgrades excluded. Reservation rules need corridor review; Hungary is treated as required despite generic table optional.

reviewedInclusionSources.quote: Between Germany and Austria: a seat reservation is optional; no supplement needed.
reviewedInclusionSources.evidence_summary: Brenner/Tarvisio Railjet Italy crossings require a supplement; domestic Italy requires both reservation and supplement on the detailed page. The broader Railjet train-type page differs on Italy details, so Italy is outside this review; no prices are inferred.

reviewedInclusionSources.quote: a pass surcharge is required on certain connections, such as ICE/TGV trains to France.
reviewedInclusionSources.evidence_summary: DB current page independently confirms French international high-speed pass surcharges in addition to seat reservations; preserve this separate obligation.

reviewedTrainFerries.meaning: Display classification of two dated source train legs carried by ferry; endpoint geometry remains approximate and is not a rail bridge.

methodology.metric: Dated scheduled source passenger-call traversals; not passenger usage or unique physical trains.
methodology.dateScope: Seven source service dates; agency-local service times. Actual running, live disruption and seat inventory are not observed.
methodology.sourceAuthority: Source/station namespaces remain separate. Declared redundant PL/DE subsets and STA aggregate are alternative tiers; this is not exhaustive cross-feed deduplication.
methodology.boarding: boardable fields require origin pickup and destination drop-off permission; request pickup remains flagged.
methodology.eurail: Only published inclusion= included enters included counts. Conditions, reservation and actual operation remain separate.
methodology.reviewedEurail: Separate reviewedEurail counts apply narrowly evidenced Global ordinary-second-class map rules. Canonical inclusion and original reservation/supplement remain unchanged; no passholder seat availability is verified.
methodology.geometry: One simplified representative path per directed source station pair; inferred/provider geometry is not exact dated track use. Schematic fallback is explicit.
methodology.hubConnections: Consecutive called city catchments on the same dated service, with ordinary intermediate calls allowed. Catchments do not establish free interchange.
methodology.journeys: Direct same-pattern ordered calls only. No connecting itinerary or live-routing claim.
methodology.footprint: Explicitly reviewed redistributable source subset; private or unreviewed sources remain outside this public bundle.

provenance.countryEvidence: Canonical ordered passenger-call evidence; alignment and station consistency validated.

countryReference.role: Analytical passenger-call country evidence; geometry is not a web asset.

borderPolicyReference.scope: Global Pass, ordinary second class. These narrow host-country rules supplement the issuer company table; they do not change canonical calls, geometry, train operation or seat availability.

sources.evidence_summary: The issuer describes Lyon-Geneva TER and Annecy-Geneva Léman Express as pass-covered alternatives without reservations.
The issuer's 2026 Swiss validity map shows the Geneva regional corridors to Annemasse, Coppet, the airport and La Plaine as included.
The 2026 operator map identifies L4 Coppet-Annemasse, L7 Geneva Airport/Vernier-Annemasse, and Geneva-Bellegarde regional trains towards Lyon, Grenoble and Valence.
The operator identifies RE33 Annemasse-Geneva-Martigny-St-Maurice. The issuer's 2026 validity map includes the Annemasse-Geneva corridor.
The issuer includes Zurich S-Bahn except S4, S10 and S18. This extension is restricted to the independently identified SBB S9 corridor.
The municipality identifies S9 Schaffhausen-Uster via Jestetten, Lottstetten, Rafz and Zurich.
CFL identifies its cross-border Coradia service to Arlon and SNCB responsibility on the Belgian section. Both named national carrier/product inventories are included by the issuer.
SNCF TER and Léman Express, Luxembourg CFL Regionalbahn/Intercity, and Belgian SNCB local/Intercity are included in the Global Pass column.
